label: physical characteristics of a person: tall, short, thin
note: Chapter 101. THE OLD NOTE WAS ACCURATE, verified before drafting for the second point running: valiya and cheriya are the only size adjectives taught, they do describe things, and kuriya, melinja, thadicha, uyaram, pokkam, uyaramulla and neelamulla all return ZERO on a token-bounded sweep. TALL IS REACHED BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE, AND THAT IS THE CHAPTER'S POINT. Malayalam's ordinary word for tall is uyaramulla, which needs the relative participle uLLa -- taught NOWHERE, zero occurrences. Rather than smuggle it in, the chapter teaches uyaram as a NOUN and reaches tall through the dative-existential the learner already owns: ML-C32-undu (650) states undu as 'there is / someone has' outright, and ML-C06-dative-subject (330) owns enikku, so enikku uyaramuNTu is built entirely from taught pieces. The lesson's literal gloss, 'to me height there-is', is the honest one: a bare dative-existential is nearer 'I have height' than the idiomatic tall, which usually carries a degree word, and pokkam is the commoner noun for a person's stature. The chapter claims what it can BUILD, not that it has built the idiom. Same refusal as ozhivusamayam in chapter 98; dharikkuka (to wear) was refused on the same ground in chapter 100. NO NEW GRAMMAR: the three adjectives sit in ML-C42's frame, and uyaram's join is the anusvara taking its full letter BEFORE aaNu and undu -- scoped, because the first draft said the anusvara does that 'always, when something follows it', which ML-C96-eluppam and ML-C97-alla-sundaram both deny in as many words and which this chapter's OWN recall romanization refutes: uyaram + um is uyaravuM, with a va. THE REAL TEACHING IS THAT ADJACENT WORDS ARE NOT SYNONYMS -- cheriya and kuriya differ only in their FIRST SYLLABLE (che against ku, which is TWO characters, not one) and do not mean the same thing, small against short, and tall is the mirror of neither. REVIEW CORRECTED THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS CLAIM, which said cheriya is for OBJECTS and kuriya for PEOPLE. That is false of both words AND it contradicted a merged lesson: ML-C42-small (1020) tells the learner to put cheriya 'in front of a word you already know', and by 1020 they own kutti (810) -- so the book had already invited cheriya kutti, which this chapter was about to declare impossible. TWO INVENTIONS WERE CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT BY A TOKEN SWEEP RATHER THAN BY READING: aaL (person) was written into an example and is taught nowhere, replaced by kutti; and sahOdaran was about to be quoted in Malayalam SCRIPT from ML-C32-undu, which gives that example only in ROMANIZATION, so the borrowed example was dropped rather than imported. A whole-token owner sweep now runs over every new file before commit.
